question_text: According to the course material, BUS205 Introduction to Business is a first semester, two credit course available for:
option_a: 200 level students of B.Sc. Business Administration
explanation: The guide states BUS205 is a first-semester, two-credit course for 200-level B.Sc. Business Administration students.

question_text: According to Hartzell (2006), cited in the course material, modern writers such as Fayol, Koontz, Alleri and Perry hold that between management and administration there is:
option_a: no real distinction between the two terms
option_b: a complete legal ban on using both words
explanation: According to most modern writers like Fayol, Koontz, Alleri and Perry, there is no real distinction between the two terms.

question_text: According to Hartzell (2006), cited in the course material, administration's main functions include the formulation of broad objectives, plans and policies, whereas the main function of management is:
option_a: getting the work done through others in order to achieve the set goals
option_b: only drafting the memorandum of association
option_c: only selling shares to the public
explanation: Administration formulates broad objectives, plans and policies; management gets the work done through others to achieve the set goals.

question_text: According to Hartzell (2006), cited in the course material, administration is basically a policy and decision-making function while management is:
explanation: Administration is policy and decision-making; management is an executive function.

question_text: According to Hartzell (2006), cited in the course material, administration decides what is to be done and when it is to be done, whereas management decides:
option_a: who has to do it and how
explanation: Administration decides what and when; management decides who and how.

question_text: According to Hartzell (2006), cited in the course material, administration is important at the top levels of management whereas management is more important at:
explanation: Administration is important at the top; management is more important at middle levels.

question_text: According to the course material, the term administration is commonly used for non-business institutions whereas the term management is used for:
explanation: Administration is commonly used for non-business institutions; management is used for business enterprises.

question_text: According to Carol (1993), cited in the course material, a sole trader is a person who enters business working for himself or herself, puts in the capital, works alone or with employees, and as a reward receives:
option_d: only wages paid by a partner
explanation: Carol: a sole trader puts in the capital, works alone or with employees, and receives the profit.

question_text: According to Denedo (2004), cited in the course material, a sole trader is a form of business enterprise in which:
option_a: one man owns and manages the business
option_b: at least seven people must own it
explanation: Denedo: a sole trader is a form in which one man owns and manages the business. Also called one-man business or sole proprietor.

question_text: According to the course material, sole trading is mostly found in retailing, is the oldest type of business in Nigeria, and the sole trader is at the same time capitalist, labourer, entrepreneur and:
option_c: only a shareholder of a public company
explanation: He owns and takes profit (capitalist), does the work (labourer), takes the risk (entrepreneur) and controls operations (manager).

question_text: According to the course material, a feature of a sole trader is that liability is unlimited, meaning if the owner is indebted:
option_a: both the business asset and his personal asset can be sold to offset the debt
option_b: only the company's share capital can be touched
option_c: personal assets are always protected by statute
explanation: Unlimited liability: both business and personal assets can be sold to offset the debt.

question_text: According to the course material, a sole trader is not a legal entity: by law the business and the owner are regarded as:
explanation: It is not a legal entity. The business and the owner are regarded as one person.

question_text: According to Denedo (2004), cited in the course material, partnership is an association of two to twenty persons carrying on a business in common with the view of making profit, except that for a bank it is:
explanation: Partnership is 2-20 persons, or 2-10 persons in the case of a bank.

question_text: According to the course material, features of partnership include that liability is unlimited except for limited partners, it has no separate legal entity, and it has:
option_c: unlimited liability for every limited partner
explanation: Partnership has no separate legal entity and no board of directors. Capital withdrawal must be approved as in the partnership deed.

question_text: According to the course material, in ordinary partnership all members take active part in management and are generally liable, while in limited partnership there is at least one ordinary partner who has:
option_c: only a guarantee to a church
explanation: In limited partnership, at least one ordinary partner has unlimited liability; a limited partner's debt is restricted to the amount contributed.

question_text: According to the course material, an active partner takes part in formation, financing and management and may receive salary as manager or director as spelt out in the partnership deed, whereas a dormant or sleeping partner:
option_a: contributes but does not take an active management role
option_c: owns a public company by law
explanation: Active partners manage; dormant/sleeping partners contribute without taking an active management role.

question_text: According to the course material, a company is an association of individuals who jointly pool their capital to own a business distinct from others; those who buy or own shares are:
option_a: shareholders, regarded as the owners of the company
explanation: Those who buy or own shares are shareholders and are regarded as the owners of the company.

question_text: According to the course material, a private limited liability company when formed has a minimum of two people and a maximum of fifty, while a public limited liability company has a minimum of seven and:
explanation: Private: min 2, max 50 (including employees). Public: min 7, maximum not stated; people are free to buy and sell shares.

question_text: According to the course material, limited liability companies by shares means that if the company is liquidated the owners lose only:
option_a: the shares they have in the company
explanation: Liability is limited to the amount contributed; on liquidation they lose only the shares they have in the company.

question_text: According to the course material, limited liability company by guarantee is for promotion of science, religion, arts, education and not for profit making; liabilities are limited by:
option_d: the partnership deed of a bank
explanation: Companies limited by guarantee are not for profit; they source funds from members; liability is limited by promise or guarantee.

question_text: According to the course material, formation of a joint stock company starts with documents presented to the registrar of companies, including the memorandum of association, which states how the company will relate with the outside world and includes the name with:
explanation: The memorandum includes the name of the company with 'limited' as the last word, plus location and objectives.

question_text: According to the course material, line organization is the type where you have direct authority over your respective subordinates through:
explanation: Line organization: direct authority over subordinates through chain of command; managers have full authority in their area of functioning.

question_text: According to the course material, theories of management treated in the administration unit include behavioural theories, management science and:
explanation: The unit covers behavioural theories of management, management science, and the system approach.

question_text: According to Fayol, cited in the course material, all undertakings require planning, organization, command, coordination and control, and we are no longer confronted with several administrative sciences but with one which can be applied equally well to:
explanation: Fayol: one administrative science applied equally to public and private affairs.

question_text: According to the course material, sources of capital for a sole trader include personal saving, intended capital, credit, borrowing from relatives and:
explanation: Sole-trader finance: personal saving, intended capital, credit, relatives, banks.
